note: f64 bit patterns (0x%016x) and f32 bit patterns (0x%08x) are the normative fields; decimal fields are for reading and are emitted only for blocks of 32 values or fewer, plus on the split cases. Sums accumulate SEQUENTIALLY in flat row-major index order, which is what §4.2 fixes; `discriminators.numpy_pairwise_*` records what NumPy's own pairwise grouping gives instead. This file carries no version strings so that regenerating it must reproduce it byte-for-byte; the interpreter and NumPy versions are printed to stderr by the generator and recorded in .plan/evidence/QM-0121.md with this file's SHA-256.
channel_order: One pass in flat row-major index order. Element i sits at (row, column) = divmod(i, columns) and joins channel `row` when axis = rows and channel `column` when axis = columns.

cases.name: hand_computed_3x4
cases.why: Acceptance criterion 1 and TASK.md Test Cases row 1. Dyadic rationals, so every square and partial sum is exact in binary64 and the case is checkable by hand. Chosen to DISCRIMINATE: max|base| sits on a negative value at (1,0), max|delta| on a negative delta at (2,1), the deltas partly cancel, and the two blocks have different sums of squares.

cases.name: identical_blocks_3x4
cases.why: TASK.md Test Cases row 2. Counterpart == base, so every delta field is exactly zero and sum_sq_base is unchanged from the hand-computed case. Note what this case CANNOT prove: with the blocks equal, Σ base² and Σ counterpart² coincide, so it cannot tell the two operands apart. That is why row 1 exists.

cases.name: counterpart_all_zero_3x4
cases.why: TASK.md Test Cases row 3. delta == base exactly, so sum_sq_delta must equal sum_sq_base BIT-FOR-BIT (identical terms, identical order), sum_abs_delta equals Σ|base|, and max_abs_delta equals max_abs_base.

cases.name: asymmetric_2x5
cases.why: TASK.md Test Cases row 4 and acceptance criterion 2. Non-square, so reducing over the wrong axis yields 5 channels where 2 are expected. The channel COUNT alone catches a full transposition here; `square_asymmetric_3x3` is the case where it does not.

cases.name: square_asymmetric_3x3
cases.why: Acceptance criterion 2, the hard half. SQUARE, so both axes give 3 channels and a transposed implementation still returns a plausibly shaped answer; only the per-channel VALUES can catch it, and this block is deliberately not symmetric under transposition. max|base| = 128 sits on a negative value.

cases.name: f32_accumulator_would_be_wrong_64x64
cases.why: The precision discriminator. base[0] = 1024 and 4095 values of 2**-6: an f32 accumulator loses every small term and reports Σ w² = 1048576 exactly, where f64 reports 1048576.999755859375. TASK.md §Risks: 'f32 accumulation loses precision on large blocks'. This is the input that would show it.

cases.name: lcg_pseudorandom_64x64
cases.why: A realistic 4096-element pair from an integer LCG, with a second LCG stream as a +-0.001 perturbation. No value here is dyadic, so this is the case where summation ORDER matters: the numpy_pairwise_* discriminators record what a different (pairwise) grouping gives, which is the divergence `.plan/DIAGNOSTIC_ARCHITECTURE.md` §4.2 forbids by fixing the order.

cases.name: lcg_independent_counterpart_64x64
cases.why: The SAME kernel with an unrelated second operand rather than a perturbation of the first — `DIFF-001`'s checkpoint-diff shape, and the evidence for acceptance criterion 7 that nothing here is specialised to quantisation. It is also the case where the DELTA sums become order-sensitive: with O(1) deltas instead of 1e-3 ones, sequential and pairwise summation of Σ d² disagree.

cases.name: summation_order_matters_64x64
cases.why: The determinism discriminator for Σ|d|. base[0] = 2**20 and 4095 values of 2**-34 against a zero counterpart: sequentially every small term falls below the half-ulp of the running total and rounds away, giving exactly 1048576.0, while a pairwise grouping sums the small terms among themselves first and keeps them. Without this case the golden set could not tell the specified order from any other, and so would not verify §4.2 at all.

cases.name: single_element_1x1
cases.why: The smallest non-empty block. One channel on either axis, count 1, and every partial equals its single term.

cases.name: single_row_1x4
cases.why: Rank-degenerate in one direction: 1 row and 4 columns, so axis=rows gives one channel holding everything and axis=columns gives four channels of one element each.

cases.name: single_column_4x1
cases.why: The transpose of the case above, which is what makes the pair useful: the two must not produce the same answer.

cases.name: all_zero_blocks_2x3
cases.why: Both blocks entirely zero. Every partial is +0.0 and nothing divides by anything -- this kernel emits partials only, so a zero denominator is the AGGREGATION's problem, not this one.

cases.name: negative_zero_base_2x2
cases.why: Signed zeros. |-0.0| is +0.0, so max_abs_base must be +0.0 and never -0.0, and 0.0 - (-0.0) = +0.0 must not appear as a non-zero delta.

splits.name: hand_computed_3x4_split_at_row_1
splits.why: Acceptance criterion 3 on the dyadic fixture, where every partial sum is exact and the composition is therefore BIT-EXACT: composed sums land on the same bits as the undivided sums.

splits.name: lcg_pseudorandom_64x64_split_at_row_32
splits.why: Acceptance criterion 3 where the arithmetic is NOT exact. Regrouping a sequential sum at row 32 is a different association, so the composed and undivided sums may differ; composition_ulp records the measured distance in bit patterns rather than asserting a guessed tolerance.

splits.name: lcg_independent_counterpart_64x64_split_at_row_32
splits.why: The same composition with an unrelated second operand, so the DELTA sums are O(1) rather than O(1e-3) and their composition divergence is measured too. On the perturbed pair the delta sums compose bit-exactly, which would have left the delta fields' tolerance unmeasured.

refusals.name: shape_mismatch_rows
refusals.why: TASK.md Test Cases row 6 and §Error Handling: refused before any value is read, naming BOTH shapes.
refusals.detail: shape mismatch: base [2, 3] and counterpart [3, 3] must have identical shapes for a paired reduction

refusals.name: shape_mismatch_columns
refusals.why: The same refusal on the other dimension, so a check that compares only the element count cannot pass.
refusals.detail: shape mismatch: base [2, 6] and counterpart [3, 4] must have identical shapes for a paired reduction

refusals.name: empty_block_zero_rows
refusals.why: TASK.md Test Cases row 8. An empty reduction has no meaningful partials, so it is refused rather than reported as a vacuous zero.
refusals.detail: empty block: [0, 4] has no values; an empty reduction has no meaningful partials

refusals.name: empty_block_zero_columns
refusals.why: The other empty shape, so a check on rows alone cannot pass.
refusals.detail: empty block: [3, 0] has no values; an empty reduction has no meaningful partials

refusals.name: empty_block_zero_by_zero
refusals.why: Both dimensions zero: the shapes MATCH, so this reaches the empty check rather than the shape check.
refusals.detail: empty block: [0, 0] has no values; an empty reduction has no meaningful partials

refusals.name: nan_in_counterpart
refusals.why: TASK.md Test Cases row 7: refused, naming the position. `QM-0120` refuses NaN at the source; this is defence in depth.
refusals.detail: counterpart holds a non-finite value at row 1, column 1 (index 4); a non-finite weight is a finding, not something to reduce

refusals.name: nan_in_base
refusals.why: The same refusal on the other operand.
refusals.detail: base holds a non-finite value at row 0, column 2 (index 2); a non-finite weight is a finding, not something to reduce

refusals.name: positive_infinity_in_base
refusals.why: +Inf is refused on the same rule as NaN rather than propagating into an infinite sum of squares.
refusals.detail: base holds a non-finite value at row 0, column 1 (index 1); a non-finite weight is a finding, not something to reduce

refusals.name: negative_infinity_in_counterpart
refusals.why: -Inf, refused for the same reason. Note it would otherwise produce +Inf in sum_sq_delta and a finite-looking max.
refusals.detail: counterpart holds a non-finite value at row 1, column 1 (index 3); a non-finite weight is a finding, not something to reduce

refusals.name: non_finite_in_base_precedes_one_in_counterpart
refusals.why: Both blocks hold a non-finite value; the refusal must name the EARLIEST position across both, which is base at index 1, not counterpart at index 3.
refusals.detail: base holds a non-finite value at row 0, column 1 (index 1); a non-finite weight is a finding, not something to reduce

refusals.name: non_finite_in_counterpart_at_the_same_position_as_base
refusals.why: At one position both operands are non-finite; base is named, because base is checked first at each position.
refusals.detail: base holds a non-finite value at row 0, column 1 (index 1); a non-finite weight is a finding, not something to reduce

refusals.name: ragged_value_count
refusals.why: A block whose value count disagrees with its declared shape. `BlockData::new` rejects this at construction, but the fields are public, so the kernel checks it again rather than indexing out of bounds.
refusals.detail: value count disagrees with the declared shape: 6 values for a 2x4 block
